card.title: Force
card.body: A **force** ($\vec{F}$) is a push or pull produced by an interaction between two objects. It is a **vector** quantity that can change an object's velocity or deform its shape. Forces may act through contact (normal, friction, tension) or at a distance (gravity, electric, magnetic).
card.says: a force always comes from another object pushing or pulling, with both a strength in newtons and a direction.
card.from: observing how pushes, pulls, and fields change an object's motion or stretch a spring.
card.useWhen: drawing a free-body diagram: identify every object interacting with the body of interest and draw one force arrow for each interaction.
card.example: Hold a $2\text{ kg}$ book steady in your hand (using $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$): Earth pulls it downward with weight $W = mg = 2 \times 9.8 = 19.6\text{ N}$, and your hand pushes it upward with a $19.6\text{ N}$ contact force.
card.analogy: Every force is like a hand or an invisible rope attached to the object, pulling or pushing in a specific direction.
